text: India measures its air in a few hundred places. It breathes it in one point four billion. This is Albedo-Watch: a citizen-powered air-intelligence network that detects hidden pollution, traces smoke to its source, forecasts spikes seventy-two hours ahead, and puts the right action in front of the right official, in the right language.

Everything here is live. Fifty-three cities across twenty-six states and union territories. NASA satellite fire detections from the last forty-eight hours. And global atmospheric forecasts, corrected by a federated model that India's states train together.

This is Mission Control. Every dot is a city, coloured on the official Indian National Air Quality Index. The embers are satellite fires, and the cyan streams are today's real winds. Press play, and the map runs seventy-two hours into the future, so a GRAP spike shows up with its lead time, before it lands.

Detect finds what official monitors miss. Satellite fires and citizen reports are scored against monitoring coverage, and almost all of that evidence sits where no monitor exists. Each hidden hotspot is ranked by how many people live downwind, and Google Maps names the district responsible.

Anyone can be a sensor. Here, a voice note in Punjabi, recorded for this demo, reports stubble burning near Amritsar. Gemini three point seven Flash transcribes and translates it, classifies the source, and cross-checks it against NASA fires nearby. It is verified, routed to the District Collector and the Punjab Pollution Control Board, and the citizen gets a reply in Punjabi, with a voice.

Trace answers the question every city asks: where is this air coming from? Seven air parcels run forty-eight hours backwards through the live wind field, and meet the fires they crossed. The result is a transparent source breakdown, explained in plain language by Gemini. The response simulator then shows what each GRAP measure is worth, today, in this city.

One click turns a forecast into an order. Gemini drafts a GRAP-aligned action order for the responsible authority, with advisories in the state's own languages, an SMS, and a voice for helplines and community radio. An officer reviews, approves and dispatches, and every step lands on an auditable ledger.

Finally, the Model Commons. Global forecasts miss local reality; this week they over-read Delhi's fine particulates roughly three-fold. Each state trains on its own ground truth and shares only model weights. Alone, states do no better than the global model. Together, error falls by about a third, and a state that contributes no data at all still gets nearly the full benefit.

Built on Gemini, Google Maps Platform, Cloud Run and Firestore, on open NASA and Copernicus data, and designed as a digital public good that any Indian state, or any BRICS partner, can join by adding data, not code. Albedo-Watch. Every breath, traced.
